target.description: Establish a bubbling and active sourdough starter from scratch.

target.description: Perform a float test to confirm the starter is sufficiently buoyant and active.

test.instructions: Photograph a spoonful of starter floating in a glass of room temperature water.
test.passIf: The spoonful of starter floats on the surface of the water.

target.description: Mix and mature a separate levain build ready for a test dough.

test.instructions: Take a photo of the active levain at the peak of its fermentation cycle.
test.passIf: The levain is domed on top, airy, and smells pleasantly fermented.

target.description: Execute an autolyse phase and successfully integrate levain and salt into flour.

test.instructions: Photograph the mixed dough in its container after the initial integration phase.
test.passIf: The dough is cohesive with no dry flour pockets remaining.

target.description: Perform a full sequence of stretch-and-fold sets during bulk fermentation.

test.instructions: Photograph the dough after the final stretch and fold, showing increased smoothness.
test.passIf: The dough shows visible tension, elasticity, and gas development.

target.description: Determine the correct end point of bulk fermentation by monitoring dough volume increase.

test.instructions: Photograph the side of the fermentation container showing the specified percentage volume rise.
test.passIf: The dough has reached the target percentage increase without over-fermenting.

target.description: Pre-shape the fermented dough into a neat round and allow it to rest.

test.instructions: Photograph the pre-shaped dough on the workbench after its bench rest.
test.passIf: The dough holds its shape and maintains surface tension without sagging flat.

target.description: Shape the dough into a tight boule or batard and place it in a proofing basket.

test.instructions: Photograph the shaped loaf seam-side up in the banneton before cold retard.
test.passIf: The shaped dough has a taut outer skin and clean seam.

target.description: Score the chilled loaf with a razor blade to direct expansion in the oven.

test.instructions: Photograph the scored loaf immediately before loading it into the Dutch oven.
test.passIf: The score cut is clean, angled correctly, and deep enough to open properly.

target.description: Bake a test loaf in a preheated Dutch oven with lid-on and lid-off phases.

test.instructions: Photograph the fully baked loaf showing crust color and ear formation.
test.passIf: The loaf has a well-developed, deeply browned crust and a distinct ear.

target.description: Bake an open, airy sourdough loaf I am proud of using a Dutch oven.

test.instructions: Take a photo of the sliced crumb of your completed sourdough loaf.
test.passIf: The crumb displays an open, airy, and evenly aerated structure characteristic of a well-baked sourdough.

method.name: CFOP Method Progression
method.summary: A high-efficiency speedcubing method focusing on Cross, F2L (First Two Layers), OLL (Orientation of Last Layer), and PLL (Permutation of Last Layer).
rules: Practice solves using a proper speedcubing timer.
Learn algorithms in small, manageable batches rather than all at once.
Prioritize smooth turning over rushing to prevent hand strain.
Always execute F2L pairs look-ahead to eliminate pauses.
Record times accurately and discard the best and worst solves when calculating an average of 5.
Dedicate at least 15 minutes of every session to targeted F2L practice.
